title: Elasticity Hub: single-pane controls for Dedicated capacity health, burst & autoscale
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Operators lack a compact, actionable control surface that ties GPU pool health, burst credits, and autoscaling rules together. Current Dedicated console pages are siloed (metrics, scaling policy editor, cost estimate) — customers ask for a single place to triage performance, run temporary bursts, and preview cost impact before applying policy changes.\n\nGoal: Design an "Elasticity Hub" in the Redwood Console that: consolidates critical per-pool signals (health band, utilization, P95 latency), surfaces burst capacity/credits and warmup time, offers a safe quick-burst action, and provides an inline autoscale policy editor with cost-preview and canary rollout options. The surface must be compact (fits as a 1-row or 2-row panel on the cluster overview) and support deep dive links to the full metrics and runbook pages.
acceptance_criteria:
- Single-pane Elasticity Hub mockups (desktop & tablet) reviewed and approved by PM + Eng.
- Inline autoscale policy editor flows with preview and canary rollout UX defined.
- Cost-preview shows estimated delta for 1-hour burst, 24-hour policy change, and monthly projected cost.
- Health band visualization with 3 states (Healthy / At-risk / Critical) and a short explanation tooltip.
- Prototype clickable from hub -> expand to full-screen editor -> confirm modal.
- Design tokens and accessible color contrast validated against AA.
- Handoff spec for ENG-1987 and ENG-2045 with interaction notes and assets uploaded.
design_notes:
- Health band: small stacked bar combining utilization (sparkline), active jobs (mini bar), and P95 latency indicator. Use a 3-color band (green/amber/red) with microcopy estimating "time-to-risk" based on short-term trend.
- Burst widget: displays available "burst credits" (integer), estimated warmup time (mm:ss), and cost-per-minute for the burst. Add a 'Quick Burst' button that opens a safety modal requiring confirmation and a billing preview.
- Autoscale editor: inline rules editor with recommended presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive). Each preset shows expected throughput delta and cost delta. Provide a canary toggle (percentage of traffic or percentage of capacity) and a fallback policy button that auto-rolls back on SLO violation.
- Cost preview: show tokenized cost line items: GPU-minutes, instance-hours, and inferred network cost. Use relative sparklines to show delta vs baseline.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions in editor, clear focus states, and ARIA labels for status badges.
- Layout: default compressed state for dashboard (panel width ~650px), expand to full modal for editing. Keep primary CTA on the right (Apply / Start Burst).
- Telemetry hooks: attach event ids for 'open-burst', 'confirm-burst', 'apply-policy-preview', 'start-canary'.

Implementation considerations for Eng: we assume 1-minute aggregated metrics to reduce telemetry load; warmup estimation uses recent historical scaling events (last 3 rolling windows).
review_feedback:
- Priya Kumar (PM): 'Love the single-pane approach. We need explicit tenant isolation notes for multi-tenant pools and to call out which costs are billable to the customer vs internal amortized costs.'
- Lucas Wang (Eng - Runtime): 'We can support the UI but metrics at 1s will not be available; confirm fallback to 1m aggregates. Also need API contract for burst credits/remaining that can be stale up to 30s.'
- Nora Patel (SRE): 'Add a suggested runbook quick-link and 'suggested mitigation' one-click actions (drain-routing / add-slip-capacity) for At-risk state.'
- Design critique session (08/28): 'The cost-preview is too verbose — condense to top-line delta with expandable line-items.'
decisions:
- Use 1-minute aggregated metrics as the canonical data source for the Elasticity Hub.
- Health band will use three discrete states (Healthy, At-risk, Critical) derived from utilization and P95 thresholds.
- Implement a Quick Burst flow with a confirmation modal that shows immediate cost and expected warmup. Burst action will be telemetry gated and require an audit log entry (SR requirement).
- Autoscale presets to be the default UI entry; advanced JSON editor behind an 'Advanced' toggle.
- Canary rollouts implemented as capacity percentage (e.g., 10% of pool) rather than traffic split to simplify runtime integration.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Unified surface reduces cognitive load for operators and speeds incident triage.
- Cons: Additional complexity in UI and backend contracts (burst credits endpoint, warmup estimation).
- Decision rationale: Prioritize safer, opinionated defaults (presets + canary) to lower the barrier for non-SRE customers even if power users need the Advanced editor.
- Cost preview is an estimate; accuracy depends on telemetry granularity and recent spot instance pricing — call out 'estimated' in UI copy.
next_steps:
1) Iterate hi-fi mocks per feedback and submit final Figma frames by 2025-09-05.
2) Create ENG story set for API contract: burst credits, warmup estimate, cost delta endpoint (ENG-1987).
3) Hand-off assets and interaction spec to ENG (Rafael -> Lucas) 2025-09-07.
4) Schedule runbook link authoring with SRE (Nora) and include quick mitigations.
5) Run a 2-customer usability session (internal Redwood + 1 pilot customer) before dev merge.
6) Prepare migration/feature flag plan for gradual rollout (release: console-2025.09).
